verdicts.why: Plugging or closing something tightly is a plain physical action with no attitude toward it.
Fitting battens is a technical, descriptive action carrying no judgement.
Putting an end to an activity is the plain neighbour itself; it says nothing about how the speaker feels about it.
Preventing something from happening is described neutrally; compare loaded alternatives like 'stifle' or 'squash'.
Having an end in time or space is a bare description with no attitude attached.
Holding back or checking something is plainly stated; the referent may be a danger but the word takes no side.
Stopping and waiting is a neutral description of pausing, as in the carriage stopping at the gate.
Intercepting something on its way is a plain action word with no judgement of the actor or the thing.
Blocking a passage is descriptive; no attitude beyond the meaning.
It names an unpleasant state or a regrettable thing plainly; the bad referent is the meaning, and 'unhappy' is the mild plain word beside 'wretched' or 'miserable'.
Keeping an account of something is a neutral bookkeeping action.
Freedom from doubt is a named mental state; the word does not praise or blame the person who has it, unlike 'cockiness' or 'self-assurance' in some uses.
Hopeful expectation that events will turn out well is described without the speaker taking a side on whether it is warranted.
An imperfection in an object or machine is a plain technical defect; the word is the neutral term, not a loaded one.
A geological fault is a technical term with no attitude.
An illegal serve in sport is a rule-defined term carrying no judgement of the player.
An electrical fault is a technical failure named plainly.
A legal document is a plain technical term with no attitude.
The semantic role of instrument is a linguistic label, purely descriptive.
Small sewing items and personal articles are named plainly with no judgement.
Placing things in a sequence is a neutral action.
Bringing order to something is described plainly; the word does not judge the thing ordered or the person ordering.
Arranging thoughts or events is a plain description of organising.
Assigning a rank is a neutral procedural action.
Bringing something into conformity with rules is described without approval or contempt for either the rules or the thing regulated.
